title: Two months into developing Words at War, I’m working on Episode 2
author: Bright-Management-27
selftext:
I’m about two months into making Words at War, a first-person typing shooter where every correct letter fires a shot. Episode 2, Ridgeline, is set in the northern Italian highlands in 1944. I’ve been working on it with Astra in my spare time after work, and so far that’s worked out to about one episode a month.

Episode 2 adds the game’s first boss fight. I’ve been trying different ways to make it feel distinct from a regular encounter in a typing game, and it’s taking longer than I expected.

Astra helps me prototype ideas quickly, but I still have to make the design, art, and presentation decisions myself. I have to decide what I want the fight to feel like, play through different versions, and figure out what’s worth keeping. That part is still hard.

What would you want out of a boss fight in a typing shooter? If you develop games with AI, I’d also love to hear how you make those design and presentation decisions.

Play Episode 1 for free: [Words at War on itch.io](https://studio-rhei.itch.io/words-at-war)

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body:
hah typing them to death, man thats mad, i love it. nice work.

you gotta add like a throw back the grenade typing sequence lol.

replies.author: Bright-Management-27
replies.body: Thanks! You can already toss grenades back with E, but making you type RETURN TO SENDER while one rolls toward you would be evil lol

comments.author: Birthdaybudreviews
comments.body:
You should have choices the player can make throughout by typing between two or three options, if you don't already. That way the game has more replay factor. For instance: you arrive at an enemy bunker. Do you use grenades, flamethrower, or call in an airstrike. 

Branching decisions could affect mission outcome and allow for upgrades, different weapons, and varied events.

replies.author: Bright-Management-27
replies.body: Thanks, that’s a great idea! I like the idea of using typing to choose how you tackle an encounter. I’ll try adding a few choices like that and see how they play!
